sections.title: Mental model — the hi-lo guessing game

blocks.md: **Ask a yes/no question whose answer throws away HALF the suspects. Repeat until one suspect remains.**
Dictionary hunt: open middle page — too far? whole right half dies. Too early? left half dies. You never read pages linearly; you BISECT. Binary search is that instinct, coded.

steps: Too small → everything LEFT of mid dies (lo = mid+1)
Too big → right half dies (hi = mid−1)

items.q: Why can we discard a whole half?
options: sorted order proves target lives on one side only
items.explain: Order gives certainty — no checking needed on dead side.

items.q: Doubling items 1000→2000 adds how many checks?
items.explain: Halving chain grows by one link. That's why it scales.

blocks.label: iterative binary search
blocks.py:
lo, hi = 0, n - 1
while lo <= hi:
    mid = (lo + hi) // 2
    if a[mid] == target: return mid
    if a[mid] < target: lo = mid + 1   # discard left incl mid
    else:               hi = mid - 1   # discard right incl mid
return -1                              # space empty -> absent

blocks.title: Trace: search 6 (absent) in same array — watch space die

blocks.md: **Two exits, both honest:** equal → position found; empty range → proven absent. Never loop forever: mid±1 always shrinks range.

blocks.label: recursive twin (same logic)

options: mid already tested & rejected — keep it and you may loop forever
items.explain: Infinite-loop insurance: progress guaranteed each round.

items.q: 8 items need at most how many checks?

blocks.md: Duplicates? Finding ANY match is easy; finding FIRST or LAST needs discipline: on match, don't stop — RECORD it and keep hunting that direction.

blocks.label: first occurrence

blocks.md: **Count occurrences** = last − first + 1. Two hunts replace full scans. This exact shape returns as lower_bound/upper_bound at L2.
